# Data Quality Report

**Dataset:** Indian House Price Prediction Challenge (`train.csv`), SHA-256 `b960388685fd0ce4e1935f4854fdf2256b556b7976b134d82aa4972525faa32b`
**Audited dimensions:** 29,451 rows × 12 columns (verified from the file, not assumed). Target: `TARGET(PRICE_IN_LACS)` (₹ lakh).
**Generated by:** `ml/data_audit.py` from the actual CSV. Nothing was deleted or modified by this audit.

## Verdict

**Suitable for training a residential valuation model — conditionally.** The signal is real (area/BHK/location relationships are strong and monotone), but four defects must be repaired first (coordinates, duplicates, impossible areas, raw city labels) and three structural limits cap achievable accuracy no matter the model: conflicting duplicate prices (label noise), missing price-driving attributes (no bathrooms, age, furnishing or floor), and locality-level (not property-level) coordinates.

## Defect register (every count measured)

| # | Defect | Count | Severity | Disposition (in `ml/data_cleaning.py`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Coordinate columns swapped (LONGITUDE holds latitudes) | 0 plausible as labelled; 29,193 after swap | Critical | Swap into correctly named LATITUDE/LONGITUDE |
| Q2 | Coordinates corrupt under both readings | 258 rows | High | Drop — never impute invented locations (sequential removal count: `cleaning_log.json`) |
| Q3 | Exact duplicate rows | 401 extra rows | High (split contamination: ~137 pairs would straddle a random 80/20 split) | Drop exact duplicates before any split |
| Q4 | Feature-identical rows with conflicting prices | 108 groups | Medium — irreducible label noise | Keep (documented); do not average silently |
| Q5 | SQUARE_FT field errors | max 254,545,454 sq ft; 154 rows > 20,000 | High | Drop rows outside [100, 20,000] sq ft as physical-plausibility errors (sequential removal count: `cleaning_log.json`) |
| Q6 | Target extremes | max ₹30,000 lakh; skew 17.6 | Mixed — see below | **Never delete on price.** Target is not clipped |
| Q7 | Raw CITY labels unusable as-is | 256 last-segment labels incl. states (Goa, Maharashtra) | Medium | Derive CITY/LOCALITY in the fitted pipeline; group rare labels |
| Q8 | Coordinates are locality-level | 4,116 unique pairs for 29,451 rows; one pair covers 1,009 rows | Medium | Treat coordinates as locality features, not property locations |
| Q9 | READY_TO_MOVE duplicates UNDER_CONSTRUCTION | exact complement in 100% of rows | Low | Drop READY_TO_MOVE |
| Q10 | Quasi-constant columns | BHK_OR_RK is 99.92% BHK (24 RK rows) | Low | Keep; expect near-zero signal |

## Genuine luxury vs. erroneous extremes (Q6 detail)

- Of the 100 most expensive rows, **99 carry SQUARE_FT errors** (> 20,000 sq ft) — their prices cannot be trusted *with those areas*, and they leave via Q5 (the area rule), not via any price rule.
- A genuine luxury segment exists and is retained: **160 rows** with plausible area priced above ₹1,000 lakh (median ₹45,723/sq ft).
- Most expensive plausible-area property: Breach Candy,Lalitpur — 7 BHK, 8,200 sq ft, ₹9,000 lakh (₹109,757/sq ft) — credible for a prime micro-market; deleting it would destroy real signal.
- At the cheap end, 57 of the 100 cheapest rows sit below ₹500/sq ft — flagged as suspicious, retained, and documented rather than deleted without evidence.

## Missing values

Total true nulls across all columns: **0**. Hidden text markers (empty/'NA'/'?' style) were also scanned per column — see `data_audit.json`. Zero nulls does **not** mean clean data here: the defects above are wrong values, not absent ones.

## Leakage assessment

- No target-derived column exists in the raw file (found: none). Price-per-sq-ft is computed in this audit for exploration only and is prohibited as a model feature.
- No predictor correlates with the target at |Spearman| ≥ 0.9 (found: none).
- The real leakage risk is **group-level**: exact duplicates, repeated addresses and shared locality coordinates straddling a random train/test split. Mitigation: de-duplicate before splitting and report a locality-grouped evaluation alongside the random one.

## Exclusion log (applied only by `ml/data_cleaning.py`)

| Step | Rule | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Drop exact duplicate rows | Identical in every column; keeping them contaminates any random split |
| C2 | Swap coordinate columns; drop rows implausible under both readings | Columns are verifiably swapped (Q1); corrupt rows have no recoverable location — imputation would fabricate geography |
| C3 | Drop SQUARE_FT outside [100, 20,000] | Physical-plausibility field errors (a 254M sq ft flat does not exist); price is never the criterion, so genuine expensive homes are kept |
| C4 | Drop READY_TO_MOVE column | Exact complement of UNDER_CONSTRUCTION — pure redundancy, no information lost |
| — | Target: no clipping, no deletion | The expensive tail contains genuine luxury properties (above); skew is a modelling question (log-target), not a cleaning deletion |

**Retention after cleaning** (applied by `ml/data_cleaning.py`, reconciled step-by-step in `dataset/processed/cleaning_log.json`): 29,451 raw → 29,050 after C1 → 28,795 after C2 → **28,622 retained** after C3 for this verified file (SHA-256 above).
